experiments.name: safe_handshake_and_chunk_boundaries
experiments.finding: duplicate transfers are removed; CBR line flush/padding remains absent

experiments.name: inferred_full_last_chain
experiments.finding: port names alone are insufficient to reconstruct FIFO pointer and chunk completion semantics; contract-driven retests below

experiments.name: contract_flush_enabled
experiments.finding: the muxword flush branch never triggers (the VLC pads the final word); enabling kUSE_FLUSH_LOGIC alone changes the final-group staging timing and emits 93 extra words per slice

experiments.name: contract_flush_dedup
experiments.finding: identical to contract_flush_enabled: the dedup branch never fires because i_bits_in_next_word always equals i_max_bits_per_word at line ends; kept as anti-evidence

experiments.name: contract_last_chain_no_flush
experiments.finding: restoring the downstream last propagation without the flush leaves the output identical to the safe set; the builder drops ~130 words per slice regardless, so the remaining defect is inside the stream builder / format buffer chunk logic

experiments.name: contract_line_end_direct_emit
experiments.finding: all 648 expected line-end pulses (108x3x2) reach the muxword; the word deficit (3,339 vs 3,456) therefore originates inside the muxword packing itself: the final partial word of a line is carried into the next line instead of being emitted, and the per-chunk data diverges from the golden from line 1 slice 0 (byte 254)

experiments.name: muxword_word_complete_probe
experiments.finding: bit-conserving but word-boundary-shifting: 3,297 word completions vs 3,456 expected (159 words carried across line ends); all 648 line-end pulses arrive; the RTL VLC emits line-end unit sizes that complete the word instead of leaving the 1-15 pad bits the golden expects, so the divergence originates in the VLC/rate buffer line-end bit accounting rather than format/stream framing

remaining_external_evidence: VLC line-end unit-size semantics: the RTL's dsce_vlc/dsce_muxword pair carries line-end remainder bits into the next line instead of zero-completing the final muxword; per the DSC contract each line must end on a zero-padded muxword boundary
